en: In a vacuum without air resistance, a feather and a bowling ball fall at the exact same speed.
Magnets strongly attract other metals like nickel and cobalt, not just iron.
Static friction prevents a parked car from sliding down a steep hill even when it is completely stationary.
Simple machines like pulleys do not reduce total work, but they reduce the required effort force by increasing distance.
Light takes about eight minutes to travel from the Sun to Earth, proving it does not travel instantly.
Sound waves cannot travel through the vacuum of outer space because they require a physical medium like air to vibrate.
Thermal energy always flows from a warmer object, like hot coffee, into a cooler object, like cold milk.
A lightbulb converts electrical energy into light and heat, but the electrons themselves are never used up or destroyed.
A stationary boulder resting on a high cliff possesses significant gravitational potential energy purely due to its elevated position.
When a moving car brakes, its kinetic energy is not destroyed but transformed into heat energy in the brake pads.
If you break a bar magnet in half, each new piece instantly forms its own distinct north and south poles.
A longer, gentler ramp requires less pushing force to move a heavy box upward than a shorter, steeper ramp.
